entries.title: DRAFT: outgoing rows are tilted by occupation
entries.statement: Draft campaign derivation, independent review pending. For a finite connected U containing 0 in a uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbor environment, G_U(0,x)=h/(sum_e omega(x,e) r_e), where h is the probability of hitting x before exit (h=1 for x=0) and r_e is the probability of exit before hitting x from x+e, equal to 1 outside U. Conditioned off the outgoing row at x, h and r do not use that row. Consequently spatial iid permits single-site integration but does not make G_U(0,x) independent of omega(x,.). The auxiliary row is E[G_U(0,x)omega(x,e)]/E[G_U(0,x)].
assumptions: site iid for the conditional single-site integration

entries.title: DRAFT: positive site drift can become negative occupation drift
entries.statement: Draft finite rational counterexample, independent review pending. On Z^2 sample iid rows A=(7/10,1/10,1/10,1/10) with probability 11/20 and B=(1/10,7/10,1/10,1/10) with probability 9/20, ordered +e1,-e1,+e2,-e2. The mean e1 drift is 3/50. For U={0,-e1}, the occupation mean at 0 is 2021/1581 and its drift-weighted mean is -202/2635, so the auxiliary e1 drift is -606/10105. This refutes factoring occupation and outgoing-row expectations using only iid. It makes no directional-transience assertion for this row law and does not refute the transience-ballisticity conjecture.

entries.title: DRAFT: an explicit two-type law has uniform positive auxiliary drift
entries.statement: Draft sufficient-condition derivation, independent review pending; no novelty claim. On Z^2 let iid outgoing rows be A=(7/10,1/10,1/10,1/10) with probability a>7/8 and B=(1/10,7/10,1/10,1/10) otherwise, ordered +e1,-e1,+e2,-e2. At every site of every finite connected killed domain containing 0, the Green-weighted auxiliary e1 drift is at least (3/5)(a-7(1-a))/(a+7(1-a)). This follows by conditioning off that site and using sum A_e r_e <= 7 sum B_e r_e. At a=9/10 the bound is 3/40. Exit-law matching and a bounded-jump exponential supermartingale yield (T) in nearby directions; the established iid UE (T) implication gives deterministic ballistic velocity v with v.e1>=3/40.
assumptions: existing iid UE (T) ballisticity theorem imported with its exact hypotheses

entries.title: DRAFT: local residence estimates leave a global exit-count moment
entries.statement: Scoped campaign audit. Uniform ellipticity bounds continuous residence before first exit from a set of bounded escape radius. It does not itself bound returns, an adaptively selected number of episodes, or regeneration time. For stopping-time episodes of uniformly bounded escape radius and any positive integer horizon tau, even a non-stopping horizon, finiteness of E[tau|B] is equivalent to finiteness of E[K_tau|B] for P(B)>0, where K_tau is the first episode index whose ending time reaches tau. The tower argument is made before conditioning on B. For directional regeneration the exit-count mean remains an unproved premise in this packet; almost-sure finiteness alone is insufficient.
assumptions: episode sets chosen at stopping times and fixed until exit
the C0041 parent is not proved

The sufficient local bound uses the same conditional inverse-escape tilt with a larger A-mass.
